Bee's calls to its Gnosis RPC endpoint are failing at a sustained rate. The chain-reading endpoints degrade first — /api/v1/wallet, /api/v1/chequebook/balance and /chainstate start returning "Failed to fetch ... from Swarm API" — while the rest of the gateway keeps working, so overall status stays green.

What to check, in order:
1. Which endpoint this node uses: BEE_RPC_ENDPOINT (main) or BEE_DEV_RPC_ENDPOINT (development) in /opt/swarm_connect_host.env on the host.
2. Whether both nodes point at the same endpoint. They share a public IP, so one endpoint means one rate limit, and staging load will break production. That was swarm_connect#296.
3. The node's log for the actual refusal: docker logs --since 1h <container> | grep -E '429|502|503|504'

Ignore this if the node restarted in the last few minutes — it hammers the endpoint catching up and a burst of errors then is expected.

annotations.summary: Bee node metrics not being scraped on {{ $labels.environment }}

annotations.description:
No metrics have arrived from anything for 10 minutes — not the gateways, not the Bee nodes.

This means one of two things and does not distinguish them:
  - the system really is down, or
  - the system is fine and the monitoring pipeline broke.

Either way you are flying blind. Balances, pool levels and node health are not bad — they are UNOBSERVED, which is why no other alert is firing. This is the single rule that watches for measurements stopping; every other rule stays silent when it has nothing to measure, so it cannot tell you something untrue.

Check in this order:
1. Is the gateway actually serving? https://provenance-gateway.datafund.io/health
   If that answers, the system is up and the problem is monitoring.
2. Alloy container:  docker compose -f docker-compose.host.yml ps
                     docker logs --since 30m swarm_connect-alloy-1
3. Alloy's route to Grafana Cloud (credentials, egress).

Payments were refused by the facilitator, errored with an unknown outcome, were settled without the request being delivered (refund needed), or a retry of a payment with an unknown outcome was refused (refused_after_unknown: the earlier transfer probably went through; match on the nonce). See docs/mainnet-runbook.md section 3: search data/x402_audit.jsonl for payment_settled with success=false, payment_failed stage=settle, stage=outcome_unknown_retry, and stage=delivery_after_settlement. On a test network, refusals are expected noise.

annotations.summary: {{ $labels.environment }}: {{ $labels.file }} state file not saved; changes are in memory only
annotations.description: A save of a gateway state file failed and the change is kept in memory only. The alert stays active while gateway_state_unsaved is 1, that is until a save succeeds, and for 15 minutes after any failed save. file=ownership: the ownership registry, including saves refused because the pre-migration copy could not be written; nothing retries the save, so it clears only with the next ownership change that saves. file=pool: the stamp pool state; the next sync writes it again. What a restart would lose: if only the ownership file is behind, buyers lose access to batches they paid for. If only the pool file is behind, a batch just bought for the pool can be in neither the pool file nor the pending record, so after a restart it is paid for but not in the pool; a sold batch is still not re-imported, because the ownership check (#477) stops it. If both files are behind, a sold batch can come back as pool stock and be sold again. Do NOT restart or redeploy until gateway_state_unsaved is 0 again. Read the ERROR log line ("Failed to save pool state", "Failed to save ownership state" or "Not saving ownership state"), fix the cause (disk full, or permissions on the data directory for uid 10001), and wait for the next save to succeed; for ownership, /health state.warnings is empty again once it has. See docs/mainnet-runbook.md section 4 and 5.

model.expr: (sum by (environment, host, file) (increase(gateway_state_save_failures_total[15m])) > 0) or (max by (environment, host, file) (gateway_state_unsaved) > 0)

annotations.description: A state file could not be read, and the gateway refuses what it guards until the file is restored. file=pool: pool spending is paused (no pool purchases or top-ups). pool_spend_times: the pool hourly spend record was unreadable at startup, so pool purchases are paused for an hour; it clears by itself. settlement_unknown: every paid request gets 503 PAYMENT_STATE_UNAVAILABLE. idempotency: keyed paid requests get 503 IDEMPOTENCY_UNAVAILABLE. spend_budget: stamp purchases, extensions and for-owner batches get 503 SPEND_BUDGET_UNAVAILABLE, and pool purchases and top-ups are refused internally (no response code), until the next UTC day. pool_allowance: free pool acquires get 503 POOL_ALLOWANCE_UNAVAILABLE until the next UTC day. The ERROR log names the file (and, except for pool_spend_times, its .corrupt-<timestamp> copy). Restore the file from backup, repair it, or move it away deliberately to start empty, then RESTART the gateway: the settlement_unknown, idempotency, spend_budget and pool_allowance files are read only at startup. The pool state needs no restart; it resumes after its next full sync. For spend_budget, GATEWAY_DAILY_BZZ_CEILING=-1 is a temporary override for pool purchases and top-ups, and for paid purchases, paid extensions and paid for-owner batches only where payment bypasses the giveaway budgets (mainnet, or X402_ALLOW_TESTNET_PAID_BYPASS); on a test network a paid request is charged to the caller like an unpaid one and stays refused. An unreadable ownership registry or bandwidth credit ledger stops startup instead and shows as Gateway Down. See docs/mainnet-runbook.md section 4 and 5.
